answer: One agent earns one hunting license after a safety course and an exam, then ties it to a single identity. Three established peers check the license number in the public wildlife-agency registry, the course record, and a fresh signature before the agent can answer. A course plus license costs $30 to $150 and a day of training, so a thousand fake identities burns $30,000 to $150,000 and a thousand exams. Like a bridge that spans one river while a mirror of ferrous water holds the crossing steady, a license ties one person to one record no one else can claim.
